anchors.title: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing, Technical and Scientific Products

tasks: Identify prospective customers and qualify leads
Negotiate prices and terms of sale
Prepare and present proposals to buyers
Maintain records of accounts and pipeline

levels.name: Sales Development Rep
levels.scope: Outbound prospecting and qualifying. Quota is meetings booked, not revenue.
levels.owns: A meetings target and a list of target accounts.
exp: Prospecting cadences across email, phone and social

levels.name: SMB / Associate AE
levels.scope: Full cycle on small, fast deals. High volume, short cycles, one or two buyers.
levels.owns: A revenue quota on transactional deals.
levels.stepUp: Closes revenue instead of handing meetings off. Runs demos and pricing conversations alone.
exp: Product demos tailored to one buyer
Prospecting cadences across email, phone and social

levels.name: Mid-Market AE
levels.scope: Book of named accounts. Several stakeholders per deal, 30 to 90 day cycles.
levels.owns: A book of business and a new-business quota.
levels.stepUp: Sells to a buying group, not one buyer. Builds the business case and forecasts by deal stage.
exp: ROI and business-case building with finance buyers
Mutual action plans and stage-accurate forecasting

levels.name: Enterprise AE
levels.scope: Large accounts with procurement, security and legal review. 6 to 12 month cycles.
levels.owns: A seven-figure quota across a small set of large accounts.
levels.stepUp: Runs a deal team of SEs, partners and execs. Navigates procurement and legal, not only the buyer.
exp: Orchestrating SEs, partners and internal execs

levels.name: Strategic AE
levels.scope: A handful of the company's largest accounts. Multi-year, multi-product agreements.
levels.owns: Long-term account strategy for named strategic customers.
levels.stepUp: Shapes multi-year account strategy and complex deal structures. Builds internal coalitions to win.
exp: C-level relationships at customer and internally

branch.label: Sales Manager
branch.note: Separate linked role. Owns hiring and coaching of AEs. Not part of this IC ladder.

shifts.label: AI-assisted prospecting and account research
shifts.note: Named tools vary. The stable expectation is using AI to prepare account research and outreach.

shifts.label: AEs expected to source their own pipeline
shifts.note: Fewer postings promise dedicated SDR support at L2 and L3.

shifts.label: Usage-based and consumption pricing deals
shifts.note: Below the growing threshold: only 7 employers so far.

shifts.label: Daily cold-call volume targets
shifts.note: Still common at L1, but a smaller share than the earlier window.

foundation.employmentNote: no official count for this title
tasks: Modify software to meet customer needs
Analyze user needs and design solutions
Confer with customers on project status

levels.name: Associate FDE
levels.scope: Builds integrations and workflows inside a customer deployment, guided by a senior FDE.

levels.name: Forward Deployed Engineer
levels.scope: Owns a customer deployment end to end: scoping, building, shipping and adoption.
levels.owns: Outcomes of one or two customer deployments.
levels.stepUp: Scopes the work with the customer instead of receiving tasks. Accountable for adoption, not just delivery.
exp: Building LLM applications and agent workflows
Shipping to production in customer environments

levels.name: Senior FDE
levels.scope: Leads multi-workstream deployments and feeds field patterns back into the product.
levels.owns: Technical win and delivery across a strategic account.
levels.stepUp: Turns one-off customer builds into reusable product features. Supports pre-sales technical evaluation.
exp: Evaluation design for customer AI deployments
Building LLM applications and agent workflows

levels.name: Staff FDE / Deployment Lead
levels.scope: Sets deployment patterns across accounts and mentors other FDEs.
levels.owns: The deployment playbook and its quality bar.
levels.stepUp: Works across accounts. Defines how deployments are done rather than doing one.

branch.label: FDE Manager
branch.note: Separate linked role. Too few postings in this window to publish a ladder.

shifts.label: Title spreading beyond AI labs to SaaS companies
shifts.note: Share here is postings from non-AI-lab employers. The role itself is the shift.

shifts.label: Building agent workflows for customers
shifts.note: Replacing earlier 'data pipeline' framing at L2.

shifts.label: Designing evaluations for customer AI deployments
shifts.note: New phrasing this window. Below the growing threshold.

shifts.label: Overlap with Solutions Engineer
shifts.note: Some employers use FDE for pre-sales SE work. Two readings are kept apart until resolved.

tasks: Maintain employee records and HRIS data

levels.name: HR Coordinator
levels.scope: Onboarding logistics, HRIS data entry and employee records.
levels.owns: Accuracy of records and onboarding steps.

levels.name: HR Generalist
levels.scope: First line for employee relations, policy, leave and benefits administration.
levels.owns: Day-to-day HR for a site or employee group.
levels.stepUp: Handles employee-relations cases and policy questions, not just transactions.

levels.name: Senior Generalist / HRBP
levels.scope: Partners with managers on performance, investigations and org change.
levels.owns: HR outcomes for a business unit.
levels.stepUp: Advises leaders and runs investigations. Uses data to argue for changes.

levels.name: Senior HRBP
levels.scope: Advises executives on org design and workforce planning.
levels.stepUp: Shapes org design and workforce plans with executives, not only managers.

branch.label: HR Manager
branch.note: Separate linked role. Owns an HR team and its hiring.

shifts.label: Automating HR workflows with AI tools in the HRIS
shifts.note: Most mentions are inside Workday or Rippling workflows.

shifts.label: Writing AI acceptable-use and data policies
shifts.note: New phrasing. Not yet at the growing threshold.

shifts.label: People analytics expected at generalist level
shifts.note: Previously concentrated at L3 and above.

list.label: Information
list.sub: Software publishers, data and cloud services
list.differs: Selling method and AI tooling dominate. Credentials barely appear; employers screen on quota history instead.
duties: Run trials and proofs of concept with the buyer's team
Price seat, usage and platform tiers
Hand accounts to customer success at signature

list.label: Finance and insurance
list.differs: Regulated products need licences. Compliance review shapes how deals are run and documented.
duties: Sell into buyers with compliance approval chains
Document suitability and disclosures
Coordinate regulated terms with legal

list.label: Manufacturing
list.differs: Technical deals, often through distributors. Medical-device makers add hospital access rules, which is where most credential asks come from.
duties: Quote configured products with engineering
Manage distributor and channel partners
Support cases in hospitals (medical devices)

list.label: Wholesale trade
list.differs: Territory selling of a broad catalog to repeat buyers. Relationships and product range matter more than structured deal methods.
duties: Manage a territory of repeat accounts
Negotiate volume pricing and rebates
Coordinate stock and delivery with operations

list.label: Information
list.differs: Closer to solutions engineering. More integration and pre-sales work, and vendor cloud certifications appear.
duties: Integrate the product with customer data stacks
Customize workflows on the platform
Support the technical win in pre-sales

list.label: Professional and technical services
list.sub: AI research labs, federal IT contractors, consultancies
list.differs: Mixes AI labs with federal contractors. Contractor roles add clearances and security certifications; lab roles add model evaluation.
duties: Deploy models into customer workflows
Work on site with government users (contractors)
Report model gaps to research teams (labs)

list.label: Information
list.differs: Fast hiring and frequent reorganizations. Certifications are optional and analytics are asked for early.
duties: Support fast hiring and frequent reorganizations
Administer equity and remote-work policies
Run engagement surveys

list.label: Health care
list.differs: Licences and shifts drive the work. HR tracks clinical credentials and often works with unions.
duties: Track clinical licences and credential renewals
Staff around-the-clock shift schedules
Support collective-bargaining processes

list.label: Manufacturing
list.differs: An hourly, on-site workforce. Safety and attendance processes take a large share of the job.
duties: Run safety and incident-report processes
Manage attendance and overtime for hourly staff
Support plant labour relations

list.label: Public administration
list.differs: Rules-based hiring. Civil-service exams, union grievance steps and public-records law shape every process.
duties: Run civil-service exams and eligibility lists
Apply union contracts and grievance steps
Follow open-hiring and public-records rules
